features.name: Academic preparation
features.description: Captures the level of formal technical education or degree attainment relevant to the role.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is mentioned.
Mentions a bachelor's degree or equivalent.
Mentions a master's degree.
Mentions a doctoral degree.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures direct design or ownership of agent-based systems with explicit orchestration, boundaries, supervision, permissions, or auditability.

levels.descriptor: No agent-based tooling experience is shown.
The letter mentions agents or autonomous workflows only in general terms.
The letter describes a recognizable agent architecture, typically pairing Python agents with Go services.
The letter shows deliberate control design for agents, such as permissions, auditability, bounded actions, or explicit end-to-end ownership.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures practical command of data structures and algorithms as evidenced by concrete engineering improvements.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Applied AI production maturity
features.description: Captures hands-on experience deploying AI or LLM systems in production with attention to reliability, evaluation, guardrails, or failure modes.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
Mentions AI or LLM exposure without concrete deployment detail.
Describes shipped AI features or workflows in production.
Describes shipped AI work plus evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or trustworthiness practices.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security engineering as helping developers through usable defaults, lower friction, and internal-user empathy rather than policing.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Engineering rigor and maintainability
features.description: Captures emphasis on correctness, reliability, failure-awareness, maintainability, testing, and long-term operational care in security-sensitive software.

levels.descriptor: No maintainer or operational mindset is visible.
Mentions maintenance or testing as duties but does not turn that into a design perspective.
Explicitly frames the applicant as a maintainer who values durability, inheritance, or real-world failure modes.
Uses maintenance or failure experience to explain a clear philosophy for how secure systems should be designed and operated.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter substantiates claims with named systems, mechanisms, scope, outcomes, or measurements.

levels.descriptor: Mostly offers generic assertions or checklist-style requirement matching.
Provides some specifics, but major claims remain abstract or unsubstantiated.
Gives several concrete, role-relevant examples showing what was built or changed.
Repeatedly backs claims with precise mechanisms, context, and outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to picture.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how central and substantial Go is in the applicant's real backend engineering experience.

levels.descriptor: Go is only briefly mentioned or not tied to meaningful ownership.
Go appears in recent work but not as a dominant language.
Go is clearly a main language for backend or service work.
Go is framed as the primary or daily-driver language with substantial system ownership.

features.name: Narrative coherence
features.description: Captures whether the letter reads as a connected, well-structured story or career arc rather than a pile of disconnected claims.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like disconnected bullets, fragments, or stacked claims.
The letter has some structure, but transitions or the overall arc are uneven.
The letter coherently links background, technical experience, and interest in the role.
The letter presents an especially well-shaped narrative that makes the applicant's trajectory and fit feel natural.

features.name: Narrative distinctiveness
features.description: Captures how memorable, individual, and non-templated the letter's voice, framing, or hook feels.

levels.descriptor: Highly formulaic prose with little individual voice.
Competent but generic prose with only limited individuality.
Includes a memorable framing device, belief, or personal thesis.
Sustains a distinctive, authentic voice throughout while still serving the application's purpose.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Captures ongoing attacker-minded practice outside routine work, especially through capture-the-flag competitions or similar adversarial exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional or casual CTF participation or similar practice.
The letter shows regular CTF participation or sustained offensive practice.
The letter shows strong competitive results or especially serious, ongoing offensive-security practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures responsibility for external codebases through upstream fixes, public contributions, maintainership, releases, or support for outside users.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional upstream patches or fixes.
The letter shows ongoing maintenance of a small project or recurring upstream responsibility.
The letter shows sustained stewardship of an open-source project with users, releases, reviews, or community responsibility.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical depth, scale, and self-directed rigor of side projects used as evidence of engineering initiative.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
The project mentioned is small and mainly serves as lightweight practice or curiosity.
The project shows substantial self-directed engineering with meaningful system design or operational concerns.
The project is an ambitious systems build that tackles hard distributed-systems, storage, or reliability problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation toward foundational infrastructure or tooling work whose benefits compound across many teams or products.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention foundational leverage or broader organizational impact.
Expresses a general desire for scale or impact but without a clear platform orientation.
Explicitly wants infrastructure or foundational work that benefits many teams.
Repeatedly frames motivation around downstream leverage, central-platform responsibility, or quiet improvements inherited across an organization.

features.name: Production software track record
features.description: Captures the depth of relevant professional experience building, launching, operating, and owning production software systems.

levels.descriptor: Meets the baseline only, with limited scope or a small number of launched systems described.
Shows a solid early-career record, with several years and some repeated launch or maintenance work.
Shows a strong mid-career record, with multiple launches and clear production breadth.
Presents an extensive record for this role, combining years, repeated launches, and broad responsibility across production systems.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter demonstrates Python as a serious production language for services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Role-specific fit
features.description: Captures how specifically the letter maps the applicant's background and motivation to this exact role and its stated responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: The motivation is formulaic and could fit almost any software-engineering application.
The letter shows some interest in security or Google, but the rationale is still fairly generic.
The letter gives clear, role-relevant motivation tied to the team's mission, working model, or problem space.
The letter gives memorable, well-tailored motivation that shows the applicant has thought specifically about this team's security-automation challenge.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience reviewing systems for security weaknesses through threat modeling, code review, attack-surface analysis, or remediation validation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security automation insight
features.description: Captures understanding of the role's core mission as scaling scarce security expertise through principled automation and security-at-scale systems.

levels.descriptor: Does not explicitly frame security work as an automation or systems problem.
Mentions automation as useful but without a strong view of what it scales.
Clearly frames automation as a way to reduce manual security workload or extend team reach.
Shows nuanced understanding of the role as scaling scarce security expertise through systems such as triage, structured response, or variant analysis.

features.name: Security collaboration posture
features.description: Captures willingness to learn from and partner closely with security specialists or internal users rather than working in isolation.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention collaboration with security partners.
Implies support for other engineers, but not specifically partnership with security specialists.
Explicitly states readiness to work with security engineers or build for their workflows.
Shows explicit partnership mindset plus concrete evidence of learning from, serving, or collaborating with security specialists.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: Captures the strength and relevance of formal external security certifications or other third-party security validation.

levels.descriptor: No security credential is mentioned.
Mentions a baseline credential such as Security+ or equivalent fundamentals.
Mentions a demanding practical credential such as OSCP or equivalent.

features.name: Security engineering philosophy
features.description: Captures the degree to which the letter conveys a thoughtful security-oriented worldview, identity, or authentic motivation for security work itself.

levels.descriptor: Offers no distinctive security philosophy beyond generic enthusiasm.
Shows broad positive sentiment about security or impact, but little deeper framing.
Expresses a clear philosophy about rigor, resilience, secure defaults, or invisible success.
Offers a memorable, specific philosophy that strongly reinforces fit for this kind of security work.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures experience building automation that reduces manual effort in vulnerability intake, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related workflows.

levels.descriptor: No past vulnerability-handling automation is mentioned.
The letter expresses interest in this problem, but gives no concrete example of having automated it.
A concrete example of triage, intake, routing, or report-handling automation is described.
The letter shows strong end-to-end automation of vulnerability handling, with clear workflow transformation or operational value.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures surface-level writing quality, including proofreading, spelling, grammar, and other mechanical correctness.

levels.descriptor: Frequent noticeable errors that distract and materially reduce polish.
Several spelling or typographical errors, though the message remains understandable.
Only occasional minor errors; generally polished.
Clean or nearly clean prose with no distracting mechanical mistakes.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures genuinely distinct dimensions that do not clearly belong to any of the recurring constructs above.

levels.descriptor: No additional languages are mentioned.
Mentions 1 to 2 additional languages.
Mentions 3 to 5 additional languages.
Mentions more than 5 additional languages.
